summary.short: Repeals and reenacts C.R.S. title 6, article 1, part 17 as a law on automated decision-making technology (ADMT) used in consequential decisions about consumers. Developers must document covered ADMT for deployers; deployers must give notices, adverse-outcome disclosures, data correction and human review. Attorney General enforcement; mainly from 1 January 2027.
summary.long: SB 26-189 repeals and reenacts, with amendments, C.R.S. title 6, article 1, part 17. It covers ADMT that processes personal data and materially influences consequential decisions in education, employment, residential housing, financial or lending services, insurance, health care and essential government services; listed technologies and low-stakes uses are excluded. From 1 January 2027, developers must document intended uses, training-data categories, limitations and use instructions for deployers, notify material updates and keep records for three years. Deployers must keep records for three years, give consumers prior notice of ADMT use and, within 30 days of an adverse outcome, a plain-language description, an information-request process and an explanation of rights. Affected consumers may request data correction and meaningful human review, to the extent commercially reasonable. The Attorney General must adopt rules by 1 January 2027. Violations are deceptive trade practices enforced only by the Attorney General, with a 60-day cure notice until 2030 and no new private right of action. Developers and deployers may be liable under anti-discrimination law by relative fault; indemnification for own acts is void. Insurers under C.R.S. 10-3-1104.9, HIPAA covered entities, FDA-regulated devices, FERPA and ECOA processes get exemptions or alternative compliance.

territorial_scope.description: Colorado; developers and deployers are persons doing business in Colorado, wherever located, and consumers include individuals whose access or opportunity in Colorado is evaluated by such a person.

obligations.summary: Developers must give each deployer documentation on intended and known harmful uses, training-data categories, known limitations and risks, instructions for use, monitoring and human review, and information needed for deployer disclosures; they must tell the deployer if information is withheld.
obligations.conditional_on: Only for deployer uses where the ADMT was marketed, advertised, configured, contracted, sold or licensed to materially influence a consequential decision (6-1-1702 (3), (5)); trade secrets and legally protected information may be withheld

evidence.quote: ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, A DEVELOPER SHALL MAKE AVAILABLE TO EACH DEPLOYER OF A COVERED ADMT DEVELOPED BY THE DEVELOPER, IN A FORM AND MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY UNDERSTANDABLE TO A DEPLOYER

obligations.summary: Developers must notify each deployer within a reasonable time of material updates, intentional and substantial modifications, and changes to intended use, limitations or risk mitigation; public release notes suffice if deployers get direct notice of the release.

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE TO EACH DEPLOYER OF A COVERED ADMT DEVELOPED BY THE DEVELOPER A NOTICE OF MATERIAL UPDATES, INTENTIONAL AND SUBSTANTIAL MODIFICATIONS

obligations.summary: Developers must keep records showing compliance with 6-1-1702 (version identifiers, changelogs, documentation and update notices) for at least three years after their creation, or longer if other law requires.

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE CREATION OF A RECORD REQUIRED OR CREATED UNDER THIS SECTION

obligations.summary: Deployers must keep records reasonably necessary to show compliance with part 17 for at least three years after each consequential decision, or longer if other law requires.

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER

obligations.summary: Before using covered ADMT to materially influence a consequential decision, deployers must give consumers clear and conspicuous notice of the use and of how to obtain more information; a prominent public notice at points of consumer interaction complies.
obligations.conditional_on: Creditors complying with ECOA/Regulation B (and FCRA) notices and FERPA-covered education deployers may comply through those processes (6-1-1704 (6), (9))

evidence.quote: PRIOR TO A DEPLOYER USING A COVERED ADMT TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS NOTICE TO A CONSUMER

obligations.summary: After an adverse outcome, deployers must provide within 30 days a plain-language description of the decision and the ADMT's role, a simple process to request information on the ADMT and the personal data used, and an explanation of the consumer's rights.
obligations.conditional_on: Content to be clarified by Attorney General rules (6-1-1704 (4)); alternative compliance for ECOA/FCRA creditors and FERPA deployers (6-1-1704 (6), (9))

evidence.quote: IF A DEPLOYER USES A COVERED ADMT TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION THAT RESULTS IN AN ADVERSE OUTCOME FOR A CONSUMER, THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER MAKING THE DECISION

obligations.summary: A deployer that withholds trade secrets or legally protected information from its disclosures must tell the consumer.

evidence.quote: IF A DEPLOYER WITHHOLDS INFORMATION PURSUANT TO THIS SUBSECTION (5), THE DEPLOYER SHALL NOTIFY THE CONSUMER.

obligations.summary: Deployers and developers must make the notices and disclosures required by part 17 reasonably accessible to consumers with disabilities and with limited English proficiency.

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER OR DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE THE NOTICES AND DISCLOSURES REQUIRED BY THIS PART 17 IN A MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY ACCESSIBLE TO CONSUMERS WITH DISABILITIES AND CONSUMERS WITH LIMITED ENGLISH PROFICIENCY

obligations.summary: On request by a consumer with an adverse outcome, deployers must give instructions for requesting and correcting factually incorrect or materially inaccurate personal data used in the decision (not opinions, predictions or scores).
obligations.conditional_on: FERPA-covered education deployers may comply through existing record-amendment and appeal processes (6-1-1705 (2))

evidence.quote: THE CONSUMER MAY REQUEST AND THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUEST: (I) INSTRUCTIONS FOR REQUESTING PERSONAL DATA AND CORRECTING FACTUALLY INCORRECT OR MATERIALLY INACCURATE PERSONAL DATA

obligations.summary: On request by a consumer with an adverse outcome, deployers must offer meaningful human review and reconsideration of the decision, to the extent commercially reasonable.
obligations.conditional_on: To the extent commercially reasonable; FERPA alternative compliance (6-1-1705 (2))

evidence.quote: AN OPPORTUNITY FOR MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW AND RECONSIDERATION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, TO THE EXTENT COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE.

obligations.summary: Insurers not deemed compliant through C.R.S. 10-3-1104.9 must give notice and disclosure of covered ADMT use in insurance decisions under the post-adverse outcome rules of 6-1-1704 (3).
obligations.conditional_on: Insurer is not subject to 10-3-1104.9 (insurers subject to it are deemed compliant in the practice of insurance, 6-1-1708 (1)(a))

evidence.quote: IF AN INSURER IS NOT DEEMED IN COMPLIANCE PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (1)(a) OF THIS SECTION, THE INSURER SHALL PROVIDE NOTICE AND DISCLOSURE OF ITS USE OF A COVERED ADMT

obligations.summary: HIPAA covered entities (exempt from 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1706 except for employment decisions) must give patients a general notice of their use of advanced technologies, including covered ADMT.

evidence.quote: A COVERED ENTITY SHALL PROVIDE PATIENTS WITH A GENERAL NOTICE OF USE OF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING A COVERED ADMT.

obligations.summary: HIPAA covered entities using covered ADMT to decide patient eligibility for financial assistance must disclose the ADMT's role, the information relied on, and how to request data correction and human review, in advance or within 30 days of an adverse outcome.

evidence.quote: A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES

obligations.summary: Contract terms between developers and deployers that indemnify or hold harmless a party against liability for its own acts in ADMT-influenced decisions violating Colorado anti-discrimination law are void (binds developers and deployers alike; not for developers whose ADMT was used outside its intended use if they complied with 6-1-1702).

evidence.quote: PURPORTS TO INDEMNIFY, DEFEND, OR HOLD HARMLESS OR HAS THE EFFECT OF INDEMNIFYING, DEFENDING, OR HOLDING HARMLESS THE INDEMNITEE ... THE PROVISION IS CONTRARY TO PUBLIC POLICY AND VOID.

obligations.summary: The Attorney General must adopt rules by 1 January 2027 clarifying the post-adverse outcome disclosures (personal-data content, sector guidance, describing the ADMT's role, interaction with other notice laws).

evidence.quote: ON OR BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2027, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ADOPT RULES TO CLARIFY AND IMPLEMENT THE POST-ADVERSE OUTCOME DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS SET FORTH IN SUBSECTION (3) OF THIS SECTION.

obligations.summary: The Attorney General must adopt rules by 1 January 2027 to clarify and implement the consumer rights to correction and human review.

evidence.quote: ON OR BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2027, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ADOPT RULES TO CLARIFY AND IMPLEMENT THE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION.

obligations.summary: When adopting rules under part 17, the Attorney General must engage stakeholders (consumer advocates, deployers, developers, sector regulators) through public notice, written comment and at least one public hearing.

evidence.quote: IN ADOPTING RULES PURSUANT TO THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL UTILIZE A PROCESS THAT MEANINGFULLY ENGAGES STAKEHOLDERS

obligations.summary: Before any enforcement action, the Attorney General must issue a notice of violation to the developer or deployer if it deems a cure possible (not required for knowing or repeated violations); provision repealed 1 January 2030.

evidence.quote: PRIOR TO ANY ENFORCEMENT ACTION FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ISSUE A NOTICE OF VIOLATION TO A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER IF A CURE IS DEEMED POSSIBLE BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL.

obligations.summary: Each January from 2028 the Attorney General must report at the Department of Law's SMART Act hearing on enforcement actions filed and completed, cure periods offered and not met, and violations where no cure was deemed possible, separately for developers and deployers.

evidence.quote: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL INCLUDE, AS PART OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LAW'S PRESENTATION DURING ITS "SMART ACT" HEARING REQUIRED BY SECTION 2-7-203, A REPORT CONCERNING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS BROUGHT AND CURE PERIODS OFFERED

enforcement.authority: Colorado Attorney General (exclusive enforcement through the Colorado Consumer Protection Act)
enforcement.triggered_by: Any violation of part 17, which is a deceptive trade practice (C.R.S. 6-1-105 (1)(uuuu)); disclosure and consumer-rights violations (6-1-1702 to 6-1-1705) are enforceable only by the Attorney General
enforcement.penalty_reference: Colorado Consumer Protection Act, C.R.S. title 6, article 1 (civil penalties and other relief; amounts not stated in this act). A court may treat a cure within 60 days of written notice as mitigating (6-1-1706 (3)(d)).
enforcement.cure_period: 60 days after receipt of the Attorney General's notice of violation, where the AG deems a cure possible; not required for knowing or repeated violations; 6-1-1706 (3) repealed effective 2030-01-01

evidence.quote: A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17 IS A DECEPTIVE TRADE PRACTICE AND IS SUBJECT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE "COLORADO CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT", THIS ARTICLE 1.

enforcement.authority: Courts, in actions alleging unlawful discrimination under existing state anti-discrimination laws, including the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act
enforcement.triggered_by: Unlawful discrimination arising from a consequential decision materially influenced by covered ADMT; fault allocated between developers and deployers by relative fault, no new joint and several liability; developers liable only for uses they intended, documented, marketed, advertised, configured or contracted for
enforcement.penalty_reference: Remedies under existing law, e.g. Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act, C.R.S. title 24, article 34, parts 3 to 8. Part 17 creates no new private right of action (6-1-1706 (4), 6-1-1709 (1)); private_right_of_action is coded false for that reason, although actions under existing law remain available.

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER MAY BE HELD LIABLE IN AN ACTION ALLEGING UNLAWFUL DISCRIMINATION UNDER STATE ANTI-DISCRIMINATION LAWS

"ADVERSE OUTCOME" MEANS: (a) A DECISION THAT DENIES, TERMINATES, REVOKES, OR MATERIALLY REDUCES OR RESTRICTS A CONSUMER'S ACCESS TO, ELIGIBILITY FOR, SELECTION FOR, COMPENSATION FOR, OR THE PROVISION OF AN OPPORTUNITY OR SERVICE

"AUTOMATED DECISION-MAKING TECHNOLOGY" OR "ADMT" MEANS A TECHNOLOGY THAT PROCESSES PERSONAL DATA AND USES COMPUTATION TO GENERATE OUTPUT, INCLUDING PREDICTIONS, RECOMMENDATIONS, CLASSIFICATIONS, RANKINGS, SCORES, OR OTHER INFORMATION THAT IS USED TO MAKE, GUIDE, OR ASSIST A DECISION, JUDGMENT, OR DETERMINATION CONCERNING AN INDIVIDUAL.

definitions.term: Automated decision-making technology: exclusions (listed technologies, human-review drafting tools, conversational technology not intended for consequential decisions)

evidence.quote: TECHNOLOGY THAT COMMUNICATES WITH CONSUMERS IN NATURAL LANGUAGE OR OTHER MEANS READILY UNDERSTOOD BY AN AVERAGE CONSUMER

"CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION" MEANS: A DECISION, DETERMINATION, OR ACTION MADE ABOUT A CONSUMER THAT RELATES TO THE PROVISION OF OR A CONSUMER'S ACCESS TO, ELIGIBILITY FOR, SELECTION FOR, OR COMPENSATION FOR A COVERED DOMAIN

definitions.term: Consequential decision: exclusions (low-stakes routine processes, advertising and search, fraud, AML and sanctions controls, etc.)

evidence.quote: LOW-STAKES OR ROUTINE DECISIONS, ACTIONS, AND BUSINESS PROCESSES THAT DO NOT MATERIALLY INFLUENCE ELIGIBILITY FOR, SELECTION FOR, DENIAL OF, COMPENSATION FOR, PRICING OF, OR ACCESS TO AN OPPORTUNITY OR SERVICE FOR A COVERED DOMAIN

"CONSUMER" INCLUDES AN EMPLOYEE, A JOB APPLICANT WHO IS A COLORADO RESIDENT, AND ANY INDIVIDUAL WHOSE ACCESS TO, ELIGIBILITY FOR, OR OPPORTUNITY IN COLORADO IS EVALUATED IN A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION BY A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN COLORADO.
"COVERED ADMT" MEANS AUTOMATED DECISION-MAKING TECHNOLOGY THAT IS USED TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION.

AN EDUCATION ENROLLMENT OR AN EDUCATION OPPORTUNITY; (b) EMPLOYMENT OR AN EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY THAT CREATES OR MAY CREATE AN EMPLOYER-EMPLOYEE RELATIONSHIP; (c) THE LEASE OR PURCHASE OF RESIDENTIAL REAL ESTATE IN COLORADO; (d) A FINANCIAL OR LENDING SERVICE; (e) INSURANCE
"DEPLOYER" MEANS A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN COLORADO THAT DEPLOYS A COVERED ADMT.
"DEVELOPER" MEANS A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN COLORADO THAT: ... DEVELOPS, OFFERS, SELLS, LEASES, LICENSES, OR OTHERWISE MAKES COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE A COVERED ADMT
"INTENTIONAL AND SUBSTANTIAL MODIFICATION" MEANS A DELIBERATE CHANGE MADE TO AN ADMT THAT RESULTS IN A MATERIAL CHANGE TO THE SYSTEM'S INTENDED, DOCUMENTED, ADVERTISED, CONFIGURED, OR CONTRACTED USE.
"MATERIALLY INFLUENCE" MEANS: (I) AN ADMT OUTPUT IS A NON-DE MINIMIS FACTOR THAT IS USED IN MAKING A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION; AND ... AN ADMT OUTPUT AFFECTS THE OUTCOME OF A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION
"MATERIAL UPDATE" MEANS AN UPDATE, PATCH, RELEASE, REVISION, OR NEW VERSION OF A COVERED ADMT, INCLUDING ASSOCIATED SOFTWARE, MODEL PARAMETERS, DEFAULT SETTINGS, OR DOCUMENTATION
"MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW" MEANS REVIEW BY A INDIVIDUAL DESIGNATED BY THE DEPLOYER WHO HAS AUTHORITY TO APPROVE, MODIFY, OR OVERRIDE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION

notes: Delegated or open for the resolve stage: (1) date of 'passage' for the early-effective provisions in Section 5 (2) (the bill history records final legislative action 2026-05-12 and Governor's signature 2026-05-14; the text does not say which counts as passage); (2) Attorney General rules due 2027-01-01 under 6-1-1704 (4)(b) and 6-1-1705 (3), discretionary AG rules on 'materially influence' (presumptions, examples, objective indicators) and on part 17 generally (6-1-1706 (5)(a)-(b)), and discretionary insurance commissioner rules under 10-3-1104.9 (3)(e); (3) penalty amounts, which come from the Colorado Consumer Protection Act and are not stated here; (4) links from the reenacted part 17 to us-co-sb24-205 and us-co-sb25b-004, whose bill numbers this text does not mention. Section 4 appropriates $46,190 and 0.4 FTE to the Department of Law for FY 2026-27. The developer and deployer duties apply only to covered ADMT that materially influences a consequential decision, and the developer disclosure duties only where the ADMT was marketed or contracted for such use (6-1-1702 (3), (5)). The meaningful human review definition reads 'BY A INDIVIDUAL' in the enrolled text; quoted as written.
